text:
leo_sales: Prospect (global payments) — urgent: they have a 7-year retention + legal-hold requirement for customer-managed keys. They want three options: Redwood holds escrow, Redwood stores wrapped backups, or customer BYOK with SLA for unwraps. They asked for a short risk/pricing summary.

mina_sre: Quick: plaintext escrow = no. We can support BYOK (route unwraps to customer KMS) and we can store wrapped ciphertext blobs (never unwrapped). Dedicated/Private can get SLA; hosted depends on external KMS availability. :warning:

ojas_eng: Tech nuance: wrapped-backup means customer supplies a KMS-produced ciphertext blob (e.g., AWS KMS ciphertext or PKCS#7). We store it encrypted at rest under our envelope; we never perform unwrapping. Retrieval flow must be multi-step (authz -> approval -> deliver blob). Ask for sample blob and expected QPS.

kate_legal: Contract view: accept clauses that say "Customer retains ownership and control of key material" and "Redwood may only store wrapped ciphertext blobs and will not possess plaintext." If Redwood acts as escrowee for wrapped blobs, require retrieval authorization process, limited-use terms, and indemnity language for compelled disclosure.

leo_sales: Customer will press for Redwood to be escrowee for convenience. Can we provide a ballpark uplift?

rachel_prod: Product stance: ship as "Managed Wrapped Key Backup" enterprise add-on. Pricing model: one-time integration/onboarding fee, annual compliance surcharge, per-GB encrypted storage, and retrieval fees (standard vs expedited). Until compliance sign-off mark as "custom quote."

mina_sre: Ops checklist if we accept: HSM-envelope encryption for stored blobs, immutable audit logs, strict RBAC (no human can decrypt), retrieval multi-approver workflow, auto-retention lifecycle (7-year retention + tamper-evident deletion), and retrieval drills. SLA must include carveouts for customer KMS outages and legal process delays.

ojas_eng: Integration questions to ask now: KMS vendor (AWS KMS/CloudHSM, Azure Key Vault, Thales), wrapped blob format, unwrap QPS (peak), rotation cadence (how many rotated keys to keep), whether historical rotated keys must be retained for 7 years, and sample ciphertext. Also ask if they require retrieval attestation reports.

kate_legal: I'll draft contract snippets: (1) "Customer retains sole ownership of keys" (2) "Redwood will not possess plaintext keying material" (3) "Retrievals executed only on Customer authorization per retrieval runbook" (4) "Carveout for customer KMS downtime and legal holds."

leo_sales: Next steps I propose: (1) send prospect a short note clarifying no plaintext escrow, offer wrapped-only managed backup as add-on (custom quote; compliance review required), and Dedicated/Private for SLA-backed unwrap routing; (2) request the KMS details + sample blob + QPS + rotation cadence; (3) schedule a scoping call. Any objections?

mina_sre: No objections. I'll prepare an ops appendix (latency expectations, caching behavior, retrieval RTO, monitoring signals).

ojas_eng: I'll prepare a minimal integration test plan: `wrap/unwrap smoke`, `rotation dry-run`, `retrieval drill`, `audit-log verification`.

kate_legal: I'll circulate clause snippets and a retrieval runbook template.

sec_bot: compliance-bot: reminder — open `/new-compliance-review managed-wrapped-backup <prospect-name> <scope:retention+retrieval>` before including pricing in SOW.

leo_sales: Scheduling 30m scoping call for tomorrow 10am PT. I'll post the drafted reply + questions after the call. :thumbsup:
